title: The wine world has a new grape: Sémillon Gris is officially certified as a brand new variety with South African origins
content: <p>Malu Lambert DipWSET is a multi-award winning wine writer and critic. She was named Mont Blanc Emerging Wine Writer of the Year at the Louis Roederer International Wine Writers’ Awards in 2019 and won Veritas Young Wine Writer of the Year in 2015. As co-author of <em>Klein Constantia: The Home of Vin de Constance</em>, she received a 2023 OIV Award in Paris. Most recently she was a finalist for the Gusbourne Estate Award for Long-Form Writing at the inaugural 67 Pall Mall Global Wine Communicator Awards (2024). At home in South Africa Malu is a contributing editor for <em>House & Garden</em> and writes regularly for <em>House & Leisure</em>, <em>Winemag</em>, <em>Inside Guide</em> and other local titles. Globally, her work has appeared in <em>Jancis Robinson</em>, <em>Decanter</em>, <em>The Buyer</em>, <em>Falstaff</em>, <em>Drinks International</em>, <em>The Telegraph</em> and <em>Club Oenologique</em>. A seasoned judge, Malu is a taster for <em>Platter’s Wine Guide</em> and she has judged for Decanter, IWSC and Concours Mondial.</p>

title: Andrew Jefford: ‘Luján de Cuyo is comforting, nourishing, maternal’
content: <div class="author-description"><p>Andrew Jefford has written for Decanter magazine since 1988.  His monthly magazine column is widely followed, and he also writes occasional features and profiles both for the magazine and for <em><a href="http://www.decanter.com/" target="_blank" rel="noopener" data-saferedirecturl="https://www.google.com/url?q=http://www.decanter.com&amp;source=gmail&amp;ust=1636127504805000&amp;usg=AFQjCNGxcmapJnpHFGMAjETz__znQ1b8Bw">Decanter.com</a></em>. He has won many awards for his work, including eight Louis Roederer Awards and eight Glenfiddich Awards. He was Regional Chair for Regional France and Languedoc-Rossillon at the inaugural Decanter World Wine Awards in 2004, and has judged in every edition of the competition since, becoming a Co-Chair in 2018. After a year as a senior research fellow at Adelaide University between 2009 and 2010, Jefford moved with his family to the Languedoc, close to Pic St-Loup. He also acts as academic advisor to The Wine Scholar Guild.</p><p><strong>Roederer awards</strong> <strong>2016: </strong>International Wine Columnist of the Year</p></div>

title: 'Visiting Château Rayas made me realise there are four stages of wine appreciation'
content: <p>Matt Walls is an award-winning freelance wine writer and consultant, contributing regular articles to various print and online titles including Decanter, where he is a contributing editor. He has particular interest in the Rhône Valley; he is chair of the Rhône panel at the Decanter World Wine Awards and is the owner of travel and events company www.rhoneroots.com. </p><p>He writes about all areas of wine, but specialises in the Rhône.</p><p>Matt&#39;s latest book, The Smart Traveller&#39;s Wine Guide to the Rhône Valley, was published in September 2025.</p>

title: Margaret River Vintage Report: 2024 Chardonnay and 2023 Cabernet Sauvignon
content: <div class="author-description"><p>Cassandra Charlick is a Margaret River-based wine and travel writer and presenter who was awarded a fellowship at the 2023 Wine Writers Symposium in California's Napa Valley. In addition to <i>Decanter</i>, she reviews and writes on wine for a number of publications in Australia and also has a regular wine travel column in <i>International Traveller Magazine</i>. Off the page, she's a television presenter on Channel Nine's <i>Our State on a Plate</i>, a compere at wine functions, and hosts in-person wine and food events throughout Western Australia. Through her company <a href="http://www.earnyourvino.com/" target="_blank" rel="noopener" data-saferedirecturl="https://www.google.com/url?q=http://www.earnyourvino.com/&amp;source=gmail&amp;ust=1692187587905000&amp;usg=AOvVaw18WWjWyO-1_cMUF_2ywkRE">Earn Your Vino</a>, Cassandra also delivers immersive wine experiences throughout WA's wine regions.</p></div>

title: Pinot Progress: South American Pinot Noir finds its footing in extreme terroirs
content: <p>Amanda Barnes is an award-winning wine journalist and expert in South American wines and regions. </p><p>Based in Mendoza since 2009 she is a regular South America correspondent, critic and writer for <em>Decanter</em>, as well as other international wine publications, and she is the author and editor of the <em>South America Wine Guide</em>. </p><p>She has been awarded by Born Digital Wine Awards, Millesima Blog Awards, Great Wine Capitals Best Of and Young Wine Writer of the Year. </p><p>She has received a fellowship from the Wine Writers Symposium, a scholarship for the Wine Bloggers Conference, and the Geoffrey Roberts Award. </p>

title: Panel tasting results: Napa Valley red and white blends
content: <p>Jonathan Cristaldi is a wine writer and critic based in the San Francisco Bay Area. For more than a decade, his articles on wine, spirits and beer have appeared in a host of print and digital platforms, including Decanter, Food &amp; Wine, Departures, The SOMM Journal, Tasting Panel Magazine, Liquor.com, Seven Fifty Daily, Los Angeles Magazine, Thrillist, Tasting Table and <em>Time Out LA </em>among others. When not writing about wine, Cristaldi works as a scriptwriter on film and documentary projects with award-winning commercial photographer and director Rachid Dahnoun.</p>

title: Beyond the bubbles: Inside the lives of Champagne's cellar masters
summary: What really goes on beneath the chalk..?
content: <div class="author-description"><div>Tom Hewson writes about Champagne and sparkling wine. He authored the Tim Atkin Champagne Special Report in 2022, featuring over 600 wines and insights from five weeks spent in the region. As well as writing freelance, reviewing and presenting sparkling wines, Tom runs his own newsletter Six Atmospheres, reaching Champagne and sparkling wine enthusiasts all over the world every week.</div></div>
